label: Cross-attention versus joint attention
context: Two rows of tokens: 5 text tokens (warm #B4552F, labelled with words like 'a', 'red', 'fox', 'in', 'snow') on top, 8 image tokens (blue #0B4FC0) below. Phase 1 'cross-attention (SD 1, SDXL)': arrows only go from each image token up to text tokens; the text tokens stay frozen (draw a small lock icon); next to it a 8×5 attention matrix. Phase 2 'joint attention (SD3, FLUX)': all 13 tokens are concatenated into one sequence; arrows go both ways; a 13×13 matrix with four blocks labelled image→image, image→text, text→image, text→text fills in; text tokens now also update (they wobble/brighten). Phase 3: show the two streams keep separate weights: draw two small weight boxes 'W_text' and 'W_image' feeding Q, K, V into the shared attention. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Cross-attention versus joint attention
spec.caption: Cross-attention lets image tokens read frozen text tokens through an 8×5 matrix. Joint attention concatenates all 13 tokens into one 13×13 matrix, so text updates too. Each stream still keeps its own Q, K, V weights.
